content:
maria (AE): FYI — Acme returned the SOW with two new commercial asks that affect pricing. They added a "best available pricing" clause and a clause that effectively locks our unit price for 12 months. Need quick take from dealdesk + legal.

lee (DealDesk): can you paste the exact language? hard to advise without seeing it. :eyes:  

maria (AE): here are the snippets they sent: 
```
Section 4.2 - Pricing Guarantee: Vendor shall provide Customer with the best available pricing for materially similar service offerings provided to any other customer during the Term.
Section 4.3 - Price Stability: Vendor agrees that the per-unit price for the Services will not increase by more than 0% for a period of 12 months from Effective Date.
```

raj (Legal): this is basically an MFN-style + a 12-month price freeze. we generally avoid open-ended price parity language. proposal: convert to a targeted discount parity limited to same vertical and similar committed volume, and cap any price-change obligation to planned public list price changes with 30d notice.

lee (DealDesk): pricing impact depends on committed ARR and tier. maria, what's the expected ARR and initial term? also any co-term or true-up clauses?

maria (AE): expecting $420k ARR, 24 mo term, initial committed seats for q1 pilot then scale. no auto-true-up in redline — customer expects ad-hoc scale.

dylan (SalesOps): if we accept a 12mo price freeze we need to treat as discount entitlement — affects renewals and our ability to adjust rate card. modelling quick calc: 5% expected open-market price moves x $420k = ~$21k revenue exposure for the year. that's material for Dedicated customers.

lee (DealDesk): ask: do we have authority for a concession to remove price-raise clause and instead offer a protected discount tier (e.g., lock current per-unit rate for 12 months) with a shortfall put-back on renewal? if yes I can draft concession and approval.

raj (Legal): redline language suggestions: replace "best available pricing" with "most favorable pricing for substantially similar customers in the same industry serving comparable volume, subject to written notice of public list price changes". replace 0% freeze with "price increases limited to published list changes with 60 days notice; customer discounts grandfathered for 12 months for the committed volume only."

maria (AE): customer asked explicitly for no price increases at all for 12 months. will they accept the grandfather for committed volume compromise? leaning yes but need to check.

lee (DealDesk): if we do the committed-volume grandfather approach: we need formal approval for a custom rate card + a renewal notch that disallows stacking other promos. requires VP signoff if total concession > $15k ARR impact. please confirm baseline unit price.

dylan (SalesOps): Uploaded supporting numbers to Dealsheet: https://redwood.co/deals/ACME-123 (internal). 

ContractBot: PR-2718 created by lee for pricing exception request. Status: pending_approval. Link: https://contracts.redwood/PR-2718

raj (Legal): i'll prepare a redline with the alternative language and note the business risks. will loop in compliance if they insist on parity across industries.

maria (AE): thanks — action items: raj to send redline, lee to submit concession request (PR-2718) and route to VP if needed, i'll confirm with customer whether committed-volume wording is acceptable. target update EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
